app_headline: Live wave & swell · French Atlantic coast
intro_description: Olatu reads what the sea is doing at CANDHIS wave buoys on the French Atlantic coast — live, and across their history.
picker_map_hint: Pick a buoy on the map
cc_fresh_help: The latest reading is under 2 hours old — the station is reporting normally.
cc_aging_help: The latest reading is 2–6 hours old. The buoy reports every 30 minutes, so this is a little behind.
cc_stale_help: No reading in the last 6 hours. The figures below may be out of date; check the timestamp.
def_wave_height: Significant wave height (Hs): the mean height of the highest one-third (~top 33%) of waves — the classic "sea state" size a surfer feels. The buoy measures the whole sea state, wind-chop and swell combined.
def_max_wave: The single biggest individual wave in the 30-minute record — roughly 1.6–2× the wave height. The one to watch out for.
def_period: Swell period (peak / Th1/3): the time between the most energetic waves. Longer periods mean a more powerful, better-organised swell.
def_direction: The compass direction the dominant swell comes FROM (nautical convention). At Saint-Jean-de-Luz it usually clusters W–NW, around 290–310°.
def_spread: Directional spread: how focused versus messy the swell is. Small = one clean, aligned swell; large = a short-crested, confused sea.
def_sea_temp: Sea-surface temperature at the buoy. It is only published in the real-time feed, so the history builds up forward over time.
def_wave_vs_swell: Wave = the whole sea state (wind-chop + swell together). Swell = the long-period, organised waves that have travelled from a distant storm.
chart_temp_unavailable: Temperature data not available for this period.
chart_hover_hint: Hover the chart to read exact values
time_buoy_local: Times shown in buoy local time
glossary_intro: Plain-language meaning of every value shown. Sources: Cerema / CANDHIS.
glossary_sea_state_note: Wave-height bands — the same colours used across the charts.
glossary_direction_scale_note: The direction track and the dial tint each reading by where the swell comes from.
footer_build_title: View this deployed commit on GitHub
tide_chart_empty: No tide data for this period.
def_tide: The rise and fall of the sea driven by the Moon and Sun. It shows whether the water is rising (flood) or falling (ebb), the time and height of the next high or low tide, and the range (marnage) between them — a big "spring" tide or a small "neap" one. Predictions from api-maree.fr (IFREMER / PREVIMER).

privacy_intro: Olatu is a static website: no account, no sign-up, and no server of ours that stores your data. This page explains the little it does collect.
privacy_analytics_body: With your consent only, Olatu uses Google Analytics 4 (provided by Google Ireland Ltd.) to count anonymous visits and see which features are used. IP addresses are anonymised. The analytics script is loaded only after you click "Accept"; if you decline, no Google Analytics cookie is set and nothing is loaded.
privacy_cookies_body: If you accept analytics, Google sets its _ga cookies (up to ~13 months) to tell visitors apart. Olatu itself keeps a few technical preferences in your browser — your language, chosen buoy, theme and consent choice. These stay on your device, are not tracking, and are never sent to a server.
privacy_legal_basis_body: Audience measurement runs on your consent (Art. 6-1-a GDPR), which you can give or withdraw at any time below. The technical preferences rely on the site's legitimate interest in working correctly.
privacy_transfer_body: Google and GitHub may process data outside the European Union (in the United States) under the European Commission's standard contractual clauses.
privacy_rights_body: You can withdraw consent at any time (below) and you have rights of access, rectification and erasure. Analytics data is held by Google — see Google's privacy policy. For anything else, reach out via the Contact page.

station_pick_help: Wind comes from the nearest coastal weather station — on land, not offshore. Pick another if you prefer; your choice is remembered per buoy.
def_wind: Wind speed and the compass direction it blows FROM, from the nearest coastal weather station (a real anemometer, 10-minute mean). Crossed with the swell direction it tells you offshore vs onshore.
def_gust: The strongest instantaneous gust (rafale) in the interval — how hard it truly blows in the peaks, well above the mean wind.
def_air_temp: Air temperature at the weather station. Compare it with the buoy's sea temperature (wetsuit vs the wind on the beach).
def_rain: Rainfall accumulated over the interval at the station.
def_humidity: Relative humidity at the station. Not measured at every station.
def_pressure: Mean sea-level atmospheric pressure at the station — a falling barometer often precedes a change of weather. Not measured at every station.
def_offshore: Offshore vs onshore — the wind direction crossed with the swell direction. Offshore wind (from land out to sea, against the swell) grooms the waves clean; onshore (blowing in with the swell) blows them out. Compares the station's wind with the buoy's swell, so it's an approximation — the station is on land.
